narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

Overcast conditions are ahead today with overcast skies early, at midday, and into the evening. A high of 25°C (77°F) is forecast, falling to a low of 20°C (68°F) tonight. Thunder possible from the morning, peaking around midday. Winds show no agreed bearing early, turning W by midday with gusts up to 36 km/h (19 kt), and no agreed bearing in the evening. The UV index peaks at 7.9 today. Air quality stands at AQI 40 at Ochieng' Avenue, Kisumu Central. As of 06:01, reports through 04:00: rain from 00:00; no thunder; high so far 20°C (68°F); low so far 20°C (68°F); peak sustained 11 km/h (6 kt); sky mostly cloudy.

## Extended Outlook

Warming through Sunday, with rain and thunderstorms possible Friday and Saturday, and rain and thunderstorms likely from Sunday. Friday will be overcast with four of four models wet, thunder possible, and a high of 23–27°C (73–81°F). Saturday brings mostly cloudy skies with four of four models wet, thunder possible, and a high of 24–26°C (75–79°F). Sunday remains mostly cloudy with four of four models wet, thunder likely, a 100% chance of rain, and a high of 25–28°C (77–82°F). Monday through Wednesday stay mostly cloudy with three to four models wet and thunder likely, reaching highs of 26–30°C (79–86°F). Thursday turns partly cloudy with two of two models wet, a 100% chance of rain, thunder possible, and a high of 28°C (82°F).

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Peak CAPE ahead values reach 930 J/kg for GFS, 1130 J/kg for ECMWF, 650 J/kg for ICON, 3350 J/kg for UKMO, and 1430 J/kg for Best Match, with instability peaking at 12:00. Any thunderstorm brings the hazard of sudden gusts well above the forecast wind.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

On Winam Gulf, wind moves overnight at 8 km/h (4 kt) gusting 13 km/h (7 kt), then west-southwesterly by midday at 8 km/h (4 kt) gusting 16 km/h (9 kt), then into the evening at 7 km/h (4 kt) gusting 13 km/h (7 kt), with a peak gust of 24 km/h (13 kt). Any thunderstorm brings the hazard of sudden gusts well above the forecast wind.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1011 hPa) and highest toward the southwest (1016 hPa) — a 4 hPa spread, a moderate large-scale gradient. Pressure overhead is near-steady. Sampling is a nine-point ring at 12-degree spacing, so this locates a direction, not a centre or a front. Across 5 points, today's mean sea-level pressure sits between 1016.5 and 1018.4 hPa; near-steady over three days (+0.7 hPa). The pressure trend is +1.1 hPa.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

At Day+0, GFS holds the best rain record at 93% over the last 30 checks, though no model is meaningfully better overall. ECMWF and Best Match under-forecast daytime highs and peak wind, ICON under-forecasts highs, and GFS under-forecasts peak wind while over-forecasting highs and cloud cover. GFS does not see thunderstorms coming here. The call's 25°C (77°F) high sits between GFS at 26°C (79°F) and UKMO at 23.4°C (74.1°F), while its 18.4 mm (0.72 in) rainfall aligns near ECMWF at 16.6 mm (0.65 in) and UKMO at 17.5 mm (0.69 in). Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) forecasts a higher maximum temperature of 29.0°C (84.2°F) with thunderstorms expected. Data sufficiency is settled across 92 reviewed days with 67 checks at Day+0, 31 at Day+3, and 85 at Day+7, though KMD has fewer checks.

Sunday's call: rain, 100%, with all four models wet; highs 25 to 28°C (76 to 83°F). Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) calls it wet. At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 87% of the time over 89 checks.

Further out, temperatures and winds much the same through Thursday, with rain and thunderstorms likely Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday, and showers and thunderstorms possible Thursday. Monday: all four models wet, highs 26 to 28°C (78 to 82°F). Tuesday: all four models wet, highs 26 to 29°C (78 to 84°F). Wednesday: all three models that reach it wet, highs 27 to 30°C (80 to 86°F).

Only GFS, ECMWF and ICON reach past Tuesday. GFS and ICON are the wetter solutions from Monday to Tuesday; ECMWF and UKMO keep it drier. Thursday's call: rain, 100%, with both models wet; highs around 28°C (82°F). At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 90% of the time over 85 checks.
